Definition: What proportion of land ownership does the register cover?
Comments: Land rights study reports only about 14,000 private land titles registered and cadaster operates in practice only in urban areas, implying very limited coverage of land ownership registration (<20%).
revision_notes: Fetched the cited FERN report (Land Rights in Gabon, June 2012), which states only around 14,000 private land titles were registered nationally, the cadastre functions in practice only in urban areas (which themselves cover barely 1% of national territory), and the State retains formal control of up to 90% of land, leaving most of the population as unregistered occupiers. This is corroborated by a Lincoln Institute overview citing revenue-authority figures that only ~15,000 of an identified 40,000-45,000 cadastral parcels had been issued formal titles as of 2006. A further check found a May 2026 Gabonese press report (Infos Gabon) confirming the land administration remains largely manual and that the government has only just begun a digitalisation/modernisation partnership for the cadastre with an Ivorian technical firm (SNEDAI), indicating land ownership coverage in the register is still well under 20% and no major expansion has occurred since the original assessment. Score of 1 (<20%) is confirmed; no upgrade warranted.
revised_comments: Formal land title registration in Gabon covers a very small share of total land ownership, well under 20%. Assessments based on land tenure studies put the number of registered private land titles at roughly 14,000-15,000, against tens of thousands of identified cadastral parcels, with the cadastre operating in practice only in urban areas that make up a fraction of national territory. The State retains formal control over the large majority of land, and most of the population holds no registered title, relying instead on customary or informal occupancy. As of 2026, the government has only begun a modernisation and digitalisation partnership for the cadastre, indicating registered coverage remains limited.
